purpose: Introduce Manifest::persist(&mut self, permit: &ApplyPermit) -> Result<(), ManifestError> as a required trait method that becomes the sole disk-flush entry point for a manifest handle, strip the implicit atomic_write/self.persist() calls out of write_version, update_dependency_spec, and update_optional_dependencies on CargoToml, PackageJson, and PyprojectToml, and update apply_version_plan's existing per-entry bumps/rewrites loops to call persist() explicitly after each successful mutation call -- with zero change to loop shape, open/mutate/persist counts, or observable output. This is a pure extract-persist-from-mutate refactor: it establishes the trait shape a future, separate batching spec will build on, and carries no grouping, batching, or ordering logic of its own.
scope: crates/callisto-manifests/src/lib.rs (Manifest trait definition, ManifestCstEditor blanket impl); crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs (CargoToml::persist, write_version, update_dependency_spec -- including a new defensive self-delegation guard described in AC-008/AC-018 -- and update_optional_dependencies); crates/callisto-manifests/src/npm.rs (PackageJson::persist, write_version, update_dependency_spec, update_optional_dependencies); crates/callisto-manifests/src/python.rs (PyprojectToml gains a persist method; write_version, update_dependency_spec, update_optional_dependencies stop calling atomic_write directly; update_optional_dependencies's any_updated variable is removed per AC-019); crates/callisto-model/src/error.rs (ManifestError gains one new #[non_exhaustive]-compatible variant, InvariantViolation, used only by AC-018's defensive guard -- no existing variant is changed or removed); crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs (apply_version_plan's existing bumps loop and rewrites loop only -- no other loop in this function is touched); crates/callisto-graph/src/cascade.rs's own #[cfg(test)] module (test-only addition verifying the AC-017 cross-module invariant; solve_cascade's own production logic is unchanged by this spec); a new integration test file crates/callisto-graph/tests/apply_persist_open_count_test.rs (test-only, AC-009 check (c)); crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs's own #[cfg(test)] module (test-only additions: AC-009's two primary bumps-loop and rewrites-loop tests, and AC-011's and AC-011b's failure-injection tests); each ecosystem module's (cargo.rs, npm.rs, python.rs) own #[cfg(test)] module, limited to inserting persist(&permit) calls at existing mutator call sites that assert on-disk content, plus the new AC-018 guard test in cargo.rs's test module. WorkspaceCargoResolver (a distinct type in cargo.rs that does not implement the Manifest trait) is unchanged: its own write_version, write_dependency, and persist methods and the CargoWorkspacePackage/CargoWorkspaceDependency branches in apply_version_plan that call them are out of scope.
non_goals: No grouping, batching, path-deduplication, or reduction of open/mutate/persist counts in apply_version_plan. The bumps loop still opens once, mutates once, and now persists once per bump.writes entry; the rewrites loop still opens once, mutates once, and now persists once per rewrite entry -- exactly as many opens and disk writes occur after this change as occurred before it, for every input, including plans where multiple bumps or rewrites target the same manifest path. This 'zero write-count change' claim has exactly two disclosed exceptions, both content-identical no-op persists rather than data-loss or correctness risks: (a) PyprojectToml::update_dependency_spec's non-Range/non-Exact DepSpec early-return branch (the `_ => return Ok(())` arm), which leaves the in-memory document untouched but is still followed by the loop's unconditional persist() call, per AC-013; and (b) CargoToml::update_dependency_spec's workspace-inherited-dependency delegation branch, in the ordinary case where the handle's own path (self.absolute) is distinct from self.workspace_root.join("Cargo.toml") -- which delegates the actual write to WorkspaceCargoResolver::write_dependency against the workspace root manifest and returns without touching self.document, but is likewise still followed by the loop's unconditional persist() call on the member handle, per AC-008. In both cases the extra persist() reproduces byte-identical content at the member manifest's own path; neither introduces a new distinct disk write target, a correctness change, or a deviation from AC-009's on-disk-byte assertions. A third, narrower case exists where self.absolute DOES equal self.workspace_root.join("Cargo.toml") (the handle IS the workspace root manifest) -- that case is not a content-identical no-op; it is the silent-overwrite hazard disclosed and defended against in AC-008/AC-017/AC-018, where update_dependency_spec now returns Err(ManifestError::InvariantViolation) instead of delegating.

No change to update_dependency_spec's return type. It remains Result<(), ManifestError> on CargoToml, PackageJson, and PyprojectToml. A Result<bool, ManifestError> or any other signal of 'did this call mutate its own document vs. delegate elsewhere' is Spec B's concern (it needs this signal to decide whether a later persist in the same group is safe); this spec has no grouping decision to feed, so it must not add the machinery.

No change to WorkspaceCargoResolver::write_version, WorkspaceCargoResolver::write_dependency, or WorkspaceCargoResolver's own persist method. These are on a separate type that never implements the Manifest trait; they are called from apply_version_plan's VersionWriteTarget::CargoWorkspacePackage and DepWriteTarget::CargoWorkspaceDependency arms, both of which already persist internally exactly as before and are not touched by this spec.

No change to CargoToml::update_dependency_spec's delegation branch's own write behavior for the ordinary (non-self-referential) case: once the new guard described in AC-008/AC-018 determines self.absolute != self.workspace_root.join("Cargo.toml"), the delegation branch (constructing a WorkspaceCargoResolver and calling ws_res.write_dependency) proceeds exactly as before -- that branch's own persist-of-the-root-manifest behavior is untouched, and only CargoToml's own-document-mutation branches (the non-delegating path) are otherwise brought in line with the in-memory-mutation-only rule. Note that the surrounding apply_version_plan rewrites loop still calls handle.persist(permit) on the member CargoToml handle unconditionally after this branch returns Ok(()) (per AC-008), which performs a new, content-identical write of the untouched member manifest back to its own path, in addition to the delegation's own pre-existing write to the workspace root manifest -- see AC-008 and non_goals item 1 for the full disclosure. The one addition this spec DOES make to the delegation branch is the guard itself (AC-018): a check performed before delegation is attempted, which returns an error instead of delegating in the narrow self-referential case. This guard does not change what the delegation branch writes or how -- it only decides, before any write, whether delegation should be attempted at all.

No new test-observability counter (e.g. a persist_call_count or write_call_count static) is added anywhere. This spec does not change how many times open, mutate, or persist happen, so there is nothing new to count; a counter proving open-once/persist-once collapsing behavior is Spec B's responsibility once it actually introduces that collapsing.

No change to atomic_write's internal implementation (fsync strategy, temp-file handling, parent/grandparent directory sync) in crates/callisto-model/src/atomic.rs, and no change to any ecosystem's on-disk byte format beyond relocating an existing atomic_write (or self.persist()) call from inside a mutator to an explicit call site in apply_version_plan.

No change to plan.changelog_writes handling, plan.consumed_changesets handling, plan.pre_state_update / plan.delete_pre_json handling, or the active-ecosystem lockfile-staging logic later in apply_version_plan -- these do not call Manifest trait methods and are unaffected.

No change to any Manifest trait method other than write_version, update_dependency_spec, update_optional_dependencies, and the addition of persist -- path(), ecosystem(), role(), package_name(), current_version(), iter_dependencies(), is_publishable(), and publish_targets() are unchanged on all three types.

api_surface.name: Manifest::persist
api_surface.signature: fn persist(&mut self, permit: &ApplyPermit) -> Result<(), ManifestError>
api_surface.description: New required method on the Manifest trait (crates/callisto-manifests/src/lib.rs). Flushes the handle's current in-memory document to disk via atomic_write, using the same serialization each type already produces today (CargoToml/PyprojectToml: toml_edit::DocumentMut::to_string() with BOM re-prefixed for CargoToml if the source file had one; PackageJson: format_json_pretty over the fingerprinted indent/line-ending/BOM/trailing-newline settings). Calling persist() without a prior mutation is well-defined: it re-writes the handle's current in-memory document state to disk unchanged. persist() never mutates the in-memory document; it only serializes and writes what is already there.

api_surface.name: CargoToml::persist / PackageJson::persist / PyprojectToml::persist
api_surface.signature: fn persist(&mut self, permit: &ApplyPermit) -> Result<(), ManifestError>
api_surface.description: Per-type implementation of Manifest::persist. CargoToml and PackageJson already have a private inherent persist method with this exact body; it becomes the trait method (pub, part of the impl Manifest block) instead of a private inherent helper. PyprojectToml has no persist method today (its three mutators call atomic_write inline); this spec adds one, extracting the identical render() + atomic_write(&self.absolute, ...) sequence already duplicated across write_version, update_dependency_spec, and update_optional_dependencies into a single persist method with the same error mapping (ManifestError::Write { path: self.path.clone(), message: e.to_string() }).

api_surface.name: CargoToml::update_dependency_spec
api_surface.signature: fn update_dependency_spec(&mut self, name: &str, kind: DepKind, new: DepSpec, permit: &ApplyPermit) -> Result<(), ManifestError>
api_surface.description: Unchanged in return type and normal control flow, with one new guard inserted immediately before the existing workspace-inherited-dependency delegation branch (the self.inherited_deps.contains(&(kind, name.to_string())) check at ~cargo.rs:303). Before constructing a WorkspaceCargoResolver and calling ws_res.write_dependency, the method now also checks self.absolute == self.workspace_root.join("Cargo.toml") (i.e. this handle's own manifest file IS the workspace root manifest -- a non-virtual workspace root that is both [workspace] and [package]). If both self.inherited_deps.contains(...) is true AND self.absolute equals the delegation target, the method returns Err(ManifestError::InvariantViolation { path: self.path.clone(), message: <a message naming `name` and stating that the delegation target coincides with the handle's own file> }) immediately, without constructing a WorkspaceCargoResolver, without calling write_dependency, and without mutating self.document. This turns a scenario that cascade::solve_cascade's rewrite-construction logic never actually produces (AC-017) into a loud, immediate error rather than a silent data-loss path, per AC-008 and AC-018. When the guard's second condition is false (the ordinary case: self.absolute differs from the workspace root manifest path), delegation proceeds exactly as it did before this spec.

api_surface.name: ManifestError::InvariantViolation
api_surface.description: New variant added to crates/callisto-model/src/error.rs's #[non_exhaustive] ManifestError enum, alongside the existing Read/Write/Parse/MissingField/InvalidVersion/WorkspaceInherited/ReadOnlyFormat/DependencyNotFound/UnsupportedOperation/FormattingNotPreserved variants (all of which are unchanged). Carries a #[diagnostic(code(E027))] -- E020 is already used twice (CommandError::NotFound at crates/callisto-model/src/exec.rs:59 and VersionParseError at crates/callisto-model/src/version.rs:307); a full workspace grep for `code(E0` (excluding stale .claude/worktrees copies) confirms every code from E001-E026, E030-E053, and E060-E063 is already assigned, making E027 the lowest actually-free code -- and a Display message of the form "`{path}`: {message}". Returned only by CargoToml::update_dependency_spec's new self-delegation guard (see the CargoToml::update_dependency_spec entry above and AC-018); no other code path in this spec constructs it. Propagates to crates/callisto-graph/src/error.rs's GraphError via the existing GraphError::Manifest(#[from] ManifestError) transparent conversion -- no change to GraphError is needed.

api_surface.name: PyprojectToml::update_optional_dependencies
api_surface.signature: fn update_optional_dependencies(&mut self, updates: &[(String, Version)], _permit: &ApplyPermit) -> Result<(), ManifestError>
api_surface.description: The any_updated local boolean (currently gating an inline `if any_updated { render()+atomic_write }` block at the end of the method, ~python.rs:479-483) is removed entirely, along with the `if any_updated { ... }` block itself and its `any_updated = true` assignment inside the per-group-key loop. Document mutation (arr.replace(idx, new_req)) already only happens per-entry when a matching update is found -- any_updated never gated the mutation itself, only the write -- so removing it changes no observable in-memory behavior. After this change the method always returns Ok(()) after the mutation loop, having mutated self.document wherever a match was found and left it untouched otherwise, with zero direct disk I/O in its own body (satisfying AC-005). This avoids an unused-variable/unused-assignment warning that would otherwise survive under `just ci`'s `-D warnings` Clippy gate (AC-016) once the internal atomic_write call is deleted. Per AC-020, the permit parameter is renamed to _permit here because stripping the internal atomic_write leaves it unused; updates remains used (python.rs:416 updates.is_empty() and python.rs:456 updates.iter().find(...)) and is not renamed.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: crates/callisto-manifests/src/lib.rs's Manifest trait declares persist(&mut self, permit: &ApplyPermit) -> Result<(), ManifestError> as a required (non-defaulted) method, and the crate compiles with CargoToml, PackageJson, and PyprojectToml each providing an implementation -- omitting persist from any one of the three types' impl Manifest block is a compile error.

For each of CargoToml, PackageJson, and PyprojectToml: given a handle opened from a manifest file, calling write_version(&new_version, &permit) followed by reading the file's on-disk bytes shows the file UNCHANGED from before the call (write_version alone does not touch disk); calling persist(&permit) immediately afterward and re-reading the file shows the on-disk bytes now reflect the in-memory version change. This holds for every write_version code path exercised by the existing test suite, including CargoToml's workspace-inherited-version branch (the branch that flips inherited_version to false and pins an explicit value).

For each of CargoToml, PackageJson, and PyprojectToml: given a handle opened from a manifest file containing a dependency named 'demo-dep', calling update_dependency_spec('demo-dep', <matching kind>, <new spec>, &permit) on a non-delegating branch (i.e. not CargoToml's workspace-inherited-dependency delegation branch) followed by reading the file's on-disk bytes shows the file UNCHANGED; calling persist(&permit) immediately afterward and re-reading the file shows the on-disk bytes now reflect the updated dependency spec.

For PackageJson and PyprojectToml (the two types whose update_optional_dependencies mutates rather than always erroring): given a handle with an existing optionalDependencies/[project.optional-dependencies] entry, calling update_optional_dependencies(&updates, &permit) followed by reading the file's on-disk bytes shows the file UNCHANGED; calling persist(&permit) immediately afterward and re-reading the file shows the on-disk bytes reflect the updated entries. CargoToml::update_optional_dependencies is unaffected by this criterion since it unconditionally returns ManifestError::UnsupportedOperation without touching the document either before or after this change.

Reading the source of write_version, update_dependency_spec, and update_optional_dependencies on all three types after the change shows zero direct calls to atomic_write, ChangesetStorage::atomic_write_durable, std::fs write functions, or self.persist() anywhere in their own bodies (including every branch: CargoToml's inherited-version branch and non-inherited branch in write_version; CargoToml's Peer-kind-rejection, self-delegation-guard, workspace-delegation, and direct-document-mutation branches in update_dependency_spec; PyprojectToml's PEP-621-array and Poetry-table branches in update_dependency_spec; PyprojectToml's per-group-key loop in update_optional_dependencies, which per AC-019 no longer contains an any_updated-gated write block at all). This is a narrower claim than 'zero disk I/O reachable from these methods': it is scoped to disk-writing calls that these methods' own control flow adds directly. It does NOT prohibit -- and is not violated by -- disk I/O that occurs via delegation to WorkspaceCargoResolver::write_dependency, and ONLY that method: CargoToml::update_dependency_spec's pre-existing workspace-inherited-DEPENDENCY branch (cargo.rs:~303-307, the `self.inherited_deps.contains(&(kind, name.to_string()))` check) constructs a WorkspaceCargoResolver and calls its write_dependency method, which performs its own persist against the workspace root manifest -- unchanged by this spec per non_goals item 3. This carve-out does NOT extend to write_version: CargoToml::write_version's inherited-version branch (cargo.rs:199-216) never delegates to WorkspaceCargoResolver at all -- it mutates self.document directly (inserts an explicit pinned version into [package], sets self.inherited_version = false) and, before this change, ends with `return self.persist(permit)` at line 215, writing the handle's OWN file, exactly like every other branch of write_version. After this change, both of write_version's persist calls (line 215 and line 239) are simply removed with no exception or carve-out -- write_version calls WorkspaceCargoResolver::write_version only via the separate VersionWriteTarget::CargoWorkspacePackage arm in apply_version_plan (non_goals item 3's first sentence), never from within CargoToml::write_version itself. Disk I/O via delegation is also not violated by the caller (apply_version_plan or ManifestCstEditor) subsequently calling the handle's own persist() method after these methods return, per AC-007, AC-008, and AC-014. The goal this criterion verifies is 'no internal auto-persist of the handle's own document', not 'these methods touch zero bytes on disk ever, including via delegation to a different manifest's resolver'.

The signatures of write_version, update_dependency_spec, and update_optional_dependencies on CargoToml, PackageJson, and PyprojectToml are identical before and after this change, scoped specifically to parameter TYPES, parameter ORDER, and the Result<(), ManifestError> return type -- in particular update_dependency_spec's return type is not Result<bool, ManifestError> or any other type on any of the three implementors. This identity claim is scoped to types/order/return type only, NOT to parameter names verbatim: renaming an unused `permit: &ApplyPermit` parameter to `_permit: &ApplyPermit` (the standard Rust convention for intentionally-unused parameters, required by AC-020 in the 7 methods listed there) does not violate this criterion, since the parameter's type, position, and the method's return type are unchanged. A change to parameter TYPE, parameter ORDER, or return type on any of these methods (on any of the three implementors) does violate this criterion.

crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs's bumps loop (the `for bump in &plan.bumps { for write in &bump.writes { ... } }` block) contains, on the VersionWriteTarget::Manifest(p) arm, exactly one call to handle.write_version(...) followed later in the same arm by exactly one call to handle.persist(permit) on that same handle, positioned after the write_version call and before the loop moves to the next write entry; the version-already-matches-target skip branch (current == bump.to) does NOT call persist (no mutation occurred, so nothing to flush).

crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs's rewrites loop (the `for rewrite in &plan.rewrites { ... }` block) contains, on the DepWriteTarget::Manifest(p) arm, exactly one call to handle.update_dependency_spec(...) followed by exactly one call to handle.persist(permit) on that same handle before the loop moves to the next rewrite entry, UNLESS update_dependency_spec returns Err (covered separately by AC-012), in which case persist is not called. This holds in two distinct sub-cases when update_dependency_spec succeeds via CargoToml's workspace-inherited-dependency delegation branch: (1) the ordinary case, where the member handle's own path (self.absolute) is distinct from self.workspace_root.join("Cargo.toml") -- delegation proceeds via WorkspaceCargoResolver::write_dependency against the workspace root manifest, returns Ok(()) without mutating self.document, and the loop's persist(permit) call still fires on the member CargoToml handle even though its in-memory document was never touched: this performs a new, content-identical atomic_write of the member manifest back to its own path -- a disk write that did not happen before this change -- in addition to the delegation's own pre-existing write to the workspace root manifest. This member-manifest write is byte-for-byte identical to the member manifest's pre-call content (verified by AC-009 check (b)'s on-disk-byte assertions) and is not a correctness defect; it is disclosed here and in non_goals item 1 as a known, narrow exception to the 'zero write-count change' claim, structurally identical to PyprojectToml's non-mutating early-return case covered by AC-013. (2) The narrower, self-referential case, where self.absolute DOES equal self.workspace_root.join("Cargo.toml") (a non-virtual workspace root manifest that is both [workspace] and [package], and the named dependency is workspace-inherited against its own [workspace.dependencies]): in this case the delegation branch's write target and the handle's own file are the SAME file, so an unconditional persist() after delegation would silently revert the delegation's write with the stale pre-open document. Per AC-018, update_dependency_spec's new guard detects exactly this condition and returns Err(ManifestError::InvariantViolation) BEFORE attempting delegation, so the rewrites loop's persist(permit) call is never reached for this rewrite entry (it falls under AC-012's error-case behavior instead: the loop returns the error without calling persist, and the manifest at p is left unchanged). Per AC-017, case (2) is not constructible from a real, cascade.rs-produced VersionPlan -- cascade::solve_cascade never emits a DepWriteTarget::Manifest rewrite for an inherited edge -- so AC-018's guard is a defensive belt-and-suspenders check for a plan-construction invariant violation, not a path exercised by normal operation.

This change to apply_version_plan is observably behavior-preserving, verified without a separately-built 'before' binary. The PRIMARY evidence is TWO new tests, symmetric to each other, added to crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs's #[cfg(test)] module (neither relying on any of the four pre-existing tests named below for this core claim). Bumps-loop test: (i) constructs a VersionPlan containing a real, successful PlannedBump whose `from` version differs from `bump.to` and whose manifest is currently at `from` on disk -- i.e. current == bump.from, NOT current == bump.to, so the bumps loop's write_version(...) call actually executes rather than hitting the current==bump.to skip branch at ~apply.rs:85; (ii) calls apply_version_plan(...) and asserts it returns Ok; (iii) afterward, reads the manifest file back FROM DISK (std::fs::read_to_string or equivalent, a fresh read independent of the ApplyOutcome return value) and asserts the new version string is present in those bytes -- proving persist() was genuinely wired into the bumps loop end-to-end, not merely that ApplyOutcome.staged listed the path. Rewrites-loop test (symmetric, required in addition, covering the separate `for rewrite in &plan.rewrites` loop at apply.rs:~107-128): (i) constructs a VersionPlan containing one SpecRewrite whose `key.target` is DepWriteTarget::Manifest(p), where p points to a manifest fixture on disk holding a rewritable (non-workspace-inherited) dependency spec -- e.g. a CargoToml or PackageJson fixture with a plain `dep = "1.0.0"`-style entry, not a `workspace = true` entry -- so the rewrites loop's handle.update_dependency_spec(...) call actually executes and mutates self.document rather than erroring or delegating; (ii) calls apply_version_plan(...) and asserts it returns Ok; (iii) afterward, reads the manifest file at p back FROM DISK with std::fs::read_to_string (or equivalent, independent of the ApplyOutcome return value) and asserts the new dependency spec string is present in those bytes -- proving persist() was genuinely wired into the rewrites loop end-to-end. Both new tests are the only evidence this criterion accepts for 'persist was actually called in the bumps loop' and 'persist was actually called in the rewrites loop' respectively; ApplyOutcome inspection alone does not satisfy either. SECONDARY checks, required in addition but not sufficient on their own: (a) crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs's existing #[cfg(test)] suite -- cargo_only_bump_does_not_stage_python_lockfile, apply_is_idempotent_when_manifest_already_at_target_version, apply_returns_error_when_manifest_has_unexpected_version, and apply_stages_changeset_path_even_when_file_already_deleted -- continues to pass unmodified (no test body edits), each asserting the identical ApplyOutcome.staged contents and order, and the identical error results, as before this change. (These four tests are acknowledged to have zero power to catch a dropped persist() call on their own: two hit the idempotency skip branch that never calls write_version, one hits the error branch before any write, and one has `writes: vec![]`; they exist here only as a 'no regression in adjacent, already-tested behavior' check, not as evidence persist() was wired in -- that evidence comes solely from the new test above.) (b) AC-002 and AC-003's per-ecosystem on-disk-byte assertions hold for every write reachable from apply_version_plan (i.e. running apply_version_plan end-to-end produces the same on-disk bytes for every touched manifest path as the equivalent direct mutator-then-persist sequence asserted in AC-002/AC-003). (c) A separate new test, placed in its OWN new integration test file under crates/callisto-graph/tests/ (e.g. crates/callisto-graph/tests/apply_persist_open_count_test.rs) -- NOT inside apply.rs's own #[cfg(test)] unit-test module, because that module already contains many other tests (cargo_only_bump_does_not_stage_python_lockfile and siblings) that themselves call apply_version_plan and therefore open() in the same test-binary process; placing the counter test there would let those other, non-#[serial] tests run concurrently and pollute the same process-global counter, defeating the isolation this check exists to provide. The new integration test file calls callisto_manifests::reset_open_call_count() immediately before invoking apply_version_plan on a VersionPlan fixture covering at least one bump and one rewrite targeting distinct manifest paths, then asserts callisto_manifests::open_call_count() immediately afterward equals a fixed integer literal (one open per distinct write target in that fixture, determined by inspection of the fixture the test itself constructs -- not by running a separately-built pre-change binary). Per the #[serial] precedent in crates/callisto-graph/tests/manifest_cache_test.rs lines ~71-85 (whose own comment documents the hazard: `open_call_count`/`reset_open_call_count` are backed by a process-global counter), this new test MUST be annotated #[serial] (the serial_test crate, already a callisto-graph dev-dependency) AND must be the only test in its file that calls open_call_count() or reset_open_call_count() -- both conditions are required, matching the manifest_cache_test.rs precedent exactly (a dedicated file compiled as its own test binary, isolating it from apply.rs's unit tests and from any other integration test file), not merely 'a similar pattern'.

If handle.write_version(...) returns Err in the bumps loop's VersionWriteTarget::Manifest(p) arm, apply_version_plan returns that error without calling persist on that handle, and the manifest file at path p is left byte-for-byte unchanged on disk from its state before apply_version_plan was called.

Concrete failure injection for the bumps loop: given a manifest file at path p whose parent directory is made read-only (e.g. `chmod 0o555` on the parent directory on a Unix test runner, before invoking apply_version_plan) such that the directory already exists (so std::fs::create_dir_all(parent) inside atomic_write is a no-op success) but new file creation inside it fails, and a VersionPlan whose bumps loop reaches handle.write_version(...) successfully (current == bump.from, mutating self.document in memory) for that manifest, the subsequent handle.persist(permit) call fails at tempfile::NamedTempFile::new_in(parent) (crates/callisto-model/src/atomic.rs's atomic_write, before any bytes are written to a temp file and before any rename/replace of the target path occurs). This propagates as: atomic_write returns an io::Error; CargoToml::persist/PackageJson::persist/PyprojectToml::persist maps it to Err(ManifestError::Write { path, message }); apply_version_plan propagates it via GraphError's `Manifest(#[from] ManifestError)` transparent variant (crates/callisto-graph/src/error.rs) and returns Err(GraphError::Manifest(ManifestError::Write { .. })) without proceeding to any later bump or rewrite entry in the plan. The manifest file at path p is left byte-for-byte unchanged on disk from its content before apply_version_plan was called (atomic_write's failure point precedes both the temp-file write and the rename, so the original file at p is never touched). Bump or rewrite entries earlier in the same loop iteration order whose mutate-then-persist sequence both already succeeded remain persisted to disk from that earlier, successful write.

Concrete failure injection for the rewrites loop, symmetric to AC-011: given a manifest file at path p whose parent directory is made read-only before invoking apply_version_plan (same mechanism as AC-011), and a VersionPlan whose rewrites loop reaches handle.update_dependency_spec(...) successfully for that manifest (a non-delegating branch that mutates self.document in memory, e.g. a direct dependency spec rewrite), the subsequent handle.persist(permit) call fails at tempfile::NamedTempFile::new_in(parent) via the identical atomic_write failure point described in AC-011, before any bytes are written and before any rename occurs. This propagates through the identical chain: atomic_write's io::Error, mapped to Err(ManifestError::Write { path, message }) by the handle's persist method, propagated via GraphError::Manifest(#[from] ManifestError), and returned by apply_version_plan as Err(GraphError::Manifest(ManifestError::Write { .. })) without proceeding to any later rewrite entry in the plan. The manifest file at path p is left byte-for-byte unchanged on disk from its content before apply_version_plan was called. Rewrite (or bump) entries earlier in the same loop iteration order whose mutate-then-persist sequence both already succeeded remain persisted to disk from that earlier, successful write.

If handle.update_dependency_spec(...) returns Err in the rewrites loop's DepWriteTarget::Manifest(p) arm (for example ManifestError::DependencyNotFound when the target dependency name is absent from the manifest, or ManifestError::InvariantViolation per AC-018's self-delegation guard), apply_version_plan returns that error without calling persist on that handle, and the manifest file at path p is left byte-for-byte unchanged on disk from its state before apply_version_plan was called.

For PyprojectToml::update_dependency_spec specifically: when the new DepSpec variant is neither Range nor Exact (the `_ => return Ok(())` arm), the method returns Ok(()) without mutating the in-memory document, exactly as before this change; when apply_version_plan subsequently calls persist(&permit) on that handle per AC-008, the resulting on-disk file content is byte-for-byte identical to the file's content before update_dependency_spec was called (persist of an untouched document reproduces the same bytes), consistent with AC-009 check (b)'s on-disk-byte assertions, even though a disk write now occurs where none occurred before this change.

crates/callisto-manifests/src/lib.rs's ManifestCstEditor blanket impl (`impl<T: Manifest + ?Sized> ManifestCstEditor for T`) is updated so that update_version_cst calls self.write_version(new_version, permit) followed by self.persist(permit), and update_dependency_cst calls self.update_dependency_spec(name, kind, new_spec, permit) followed by self.persist(permit) -- each returning the persist() call's Result (or the mutator's Err immediately if the mutator itself fails, without calling persist). This preserves ManifestCstEditor's pre-existing effective contract (mutate-and-flush-to-disk in one call) even though no in-repo caller invokes update_version_cst or update_dependency_cst today.

Every call site of write_version, update_dependency_spec, or update_optional_dependencies within crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs's, npm.rs's, and python.rs's own #[cfg(test)] modules that reads the manifest file's on-disk content (via std::fs::read_to_string or equivalent) or re-opens the manifest from disk at any point after the mutator call, has an explicit .persist(&permit) call (or equivalent, e.g. through a helper that itself calls persist) inserted between the mutator call and the subsequent disk read; running `cargo test -p callisto-manifests` after the change reports zero failing tests and zero newly-ignored tests compared to the pre-change baseline.

crates/callisto-graph/src/cascade.rs's solve_cascade function (the rewrite-construction logic around ~cascade.rs:235-250) never produces a SpecRewrite whose key.target is DepWriteTarget::Manifest(p) for a dependency edge where edge.inherited is true; for every such inherited edge, the constructed RewriteKey.target is always DepWriteTarget::CargoWorkspaceDependency { root_manifest: edge.from_manifest.clone() } instead. This is verified by a new test in crates/callisto-graph/src/cascade.rs's own #[cfg(test)] module that constructs a graph containing at least one Cargo dependency edge with inherited: true and at least one Cargo dependency edge with inherited: false, runs solve_cascade (or the real entry point that reaches this rewrite-construction logic) on that graph, and asserts: (a) the resulting SpecRewrite for the inherited edge has key.target matching DepWriteTarget::CargoWorkspaceDependency { .. }, never DepWriteTarget::Manifest(_); and (b) the resulting SpecRewrite for the non-inherited edge has key.target matching DepWriteTarget::Manifest(_). This criterion documents and locks in the cross-module invariant that CargoToml::update_dependency_spec's own self.inherited_deps.contains(...) check (cargo.rs:~303) relies on: a real, cascade.rs-produced VersionPlan never routes an inherited dependency through a Manifest-targeted rewrite, so the self-referential hazard described in AC-008/AC-018 is unreachable from real planner output -- though AC-018's guard exists regardless, since this is a cross-module agreement, not something the type system enforces.

For CargoToml::update_dependency_spec: when self.inherited_deps.contains(&(kind, name.to_string())) is true (the dependency is workspace-inherited) AND self.absolute equals self.workspace_root.join("Cargo.toml") (this handle's own manifest file IS the workspace root manifest -- a non-virtual workspace root that is both [workspace] and [package]), the method returns Err(ManifestError::InvariantViolation { path, message }) immediately, without constructing a WorkspaceCargoResolver, without calling write_dependency, and without mutating self.document. This is verified by a new test in crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs's own #[cfg(test)] module that opens a CargoToml handle from a manifest file which is simultaneously the workspace root ([workspace] table present) and declares [package] with a dependency using `dep = { workspace = true }` (so self.inherited_deps contains that dependency) at the same path as the workspace root Cargo.toml. Because CargoToml::open (cargo.rs:79-87) rejects any manifest declaring `.workspace = true` (populating inherited_deps or inherited_version) unless the caller's OpenContext supplies `cargo_workspace: Some(...)` -- returning Err(ManifestError::Read) otherwise -- the test MUST construct its OpenContext as follows, mirroring the existing pattern in cargo_toml_with_workspace_version_requires_resolver_context (cargo.rs:~1335-1401, specifically the ctx_with_ws construction at ~1385-1389) and write_version_pins_explicitly_on_workspace_inheriting_member (cargo.rs:~1201-1278, the ctx construction at ~1243-1247): (1) write the single self-referential fixture file (containing both [workspace] and [package], with the [package] dependency using `dep = { workspace = true }`) to a tempdir at a path this test will treat as the workspace root Cargo.toml, e.g. `dir.path().join("Cargo.toml")`; (2) build `let inheritance = WorkspaceCargoResolver::load(&root_cargo_path).unwrap().inheritance().unwrap();` against that same fixture file, then wrap it `Arc::new(inheritance)`; (3) construct `OpenContext { workspace_root: dir.path(), cargo_workspace: Some(Arc::new(inheritance)), npm_workspace_kind: None }`, with `workspace_root` set to the fixture's tempdir root (`dir.path()`) so that `self.absolute == self.workspace_root.join("Cargo.toml")` actually holds once the handle is opened via a ManifestDecl whose path is `"Cargo.toml"`; (4) call `CargoToml::open(&decl, &ctx)` with that decl and ctx, which succeeds (unlike the no-resolver-context case in cargo_toml_with_workspace_version_requires_resolver_context) because cargo_workspace is supplied. The test then calls update_dependency_spec for the self-referentially-inherited dependency on the resulting handle, and asserts: (a) the call returns Err matching ManifestError::InvariantViolation; (b) the manifest file's on-disk bytes are unchanged from before the call; (c) re-reading the in-memory document (e.g. via a subsequent persist() and disk read, or an internal accessor used only by the test) shows self.document was not mutated by the failed call. This is a defensive check for the scenario AC-017 shows is unreachable from real cascade.rs-produced plans; it exists so that if the AC-017 invariant is ever violated by a future change to cascade.rs or a hand-constructed VersionPlan, apply_version_plan fails loudly (per AC-012, which now also covers this error) instead of silently reverting the delegation's write via the rewrites loop's unconditional persist(permit) call. In the ordinary case where self.absolute differs from self.workspace_root.join("Cargo.toml"), this guard's second condition is false and delegation proceeds exactly as before this spec (see AC-008 case (1)).

PyprojectToml::update_optional_dependencies's any_updated local variable (and the `if any_updated { render()+atomic_write }` block that consumed it, ~python.rs:479-483) is removed entirely as part of stripping the internal atomic_write call required by AC-004/AC-005; after this change, `cargo clippy -p callisto-manifests -- -D warnings` (the check AC-016's `just ci` phase runs) reports zero unused-variable or unused-assignment warnings for python.rs, and the method's per-group-key mutation loop (which conditionally calls arr.replace(idx, new_req) only when a matching update is found) is otherwise behaviorally unchanged -- the same dependency entries are mutated in self.document under the same conditions as before this change, and the method returns Ok(()) unconditionally after the loop regardless of whether any mutation occurred.

Stripping each method's own internal persist call per AC-005/AC-019 leaves the `permit: &ApplyPermit` parameter unused in its own body in exactly these 7 methods: CargoToml::write_version (cargo.rs -- both persist call sites removed, at former lines ~215 and ~239), PackageJson::write_version (npm.rs -- former persist call site at ~253), PackageJson::update_dependency_spec (npm.rs -- former persist call site at ~340), PackageJson::update_optional_dependencies (npm.rs -- former persist call site at ~362), PyprojectToml::write_version (python.rs -- former inline atomic_write call at ~212), PyprojectToml::update_dependency_spec (python.rs -- former inline atomic_write call at ~379), and PyprojectToml::update_optional_dependencies (python.rs -- former inline atomic_write call at ~480). In each of these 7 methods, the parameter is renamed from `permit` to `_permit` at both the method's own signature and every reference to it within the method body (there are none left after persist/atomic_write removal, so only the signature changes) -- this is the standard Rust convention for an intentionally-unused parameter and is required to avoid an `unused_variables` warning under `just ci`'s `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` gate (AC-016). CargoToml::update_dependency_spec is explicitly excluded from this list and keeps its parameter named `permit`: its workspace-inherited-dependency delegation branch (cargo.rs:~303-307) still passes `permit` to `ws_res.write_dependency(name, new, permit)`, so `permit` remains used in that method's body and renaming it would itself produce an unused-rename inconsistency (and would not compile as `_permit` being passed to a function expecting `&ApplyPermit` -- that still compiles, but the point of the convention is signaling non-use, which does not apply here since the parameter IS used). No other method's `permit`/`_permit` parameter is affected by this criterion.
